name: What kitchen layout changes are best for older homes in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: What kitchen layout changes are best for older Los Angeles homes with awkward walls and small rooms?
mainEntity.text: What kitchen layout changes are best for older Los Angeles homes with awkward walls and small rooms?

acceptedAnswer.text: Older homes in Los Angeles often have kitchens that were designed for a very different way of living. Narrow rooms, isolated cooking spaces, and awkward wall placements are common, so the best layout change is often one that improves flow without destroying the home’s character. Opening part of a wall, widening a doorway, adding better storage, or relocating appliances can make the space far more functional. In many cases, the key is to preserve the best parts of the house while updating the kitchen to work for modern daily life. A full open concept is not always the right answer, especially if the room is small or the adjacent spaces need some separation. A thoughtful redesign should also account for ceiling height, window placement, and how the kitchen relates to surrounding rooms. The most successful projects feel like they belong to the original home while solving current usability problems.
acceptedAnswer.description: Older Los Angeles homes often benefit from opening narrow rooms, improving storage, and rethinking appliance placement rather than simply enlarging the kitchen. The best layout change usually improves flow while respecting the home’s existing structure and style.
